sentences: I check the thermometer on the porch every morning to note the current temperature in degrees Fahrenheit.
I record the daily rainfall amount in a logbook using a cylindrical gauge placed in the backyard.
I measure the wind speed with a handheld anemometer and write down the number on a clipboard.
I observe the cloud cover and classify it as clear, partly cloudy, or overcast for my weather journal.
I step outside and note whether the air temperature is warmer or cooler than it was yesterday.
I read the barometric pressure from the wall-mounted barometer and note if it is rising or falling.
I check the humidity level on the digital hygrometer near the kitchen window each afternoon.
I look at the sky to see if there are any cumulonimbus clouds that might indicate a thunderstorm.
I scrape the frost off the car windshield with a plastic scraper before driving to work.
I listen to the radio for the forecast and write down the predicted high and low temperatures.
I measure the snow depth with a ruler stuck into the ground in the front yard after a storm.
I watch the rain fall against the window and count the seconds between lightning and thunder.
I check the dew point using a sling psychrometer and record both the wet and dry bulb readings.
I note the direction of the wind by watching the weather vane on the neighbor's barn.
I fill the birdbath with water and observe how quickly it evaporates over the course of a hot day.
I take a photo of the sunset and note the time it occurs in my daily weather log.
I put on a raincoat and boots before walking to the mailbox in the steady drizzle.
I measure the UV index with a handheld meter and write the number in my notebook.
I check the air quality index online and record the value along with the predominant pollutant.
I clear the snow from the driveway with a shovel after the overnight accumulation.
